TOUCHED AGAIN 2026-08-09 (corpus-wide `_dropped` sweep, thread 2.1, Tier-1 item #7) — three of Appendix F's four `no-node-yet` geographic/administrative leads resolved (one real node, two termini); see the corrected `_dropped` entries below.
_provenance: Adjudicated from a submitted consolidated artifact under the V0.9 rule that a second reader extracts and this project adjudicates. The artifact arrived carrying finished verdicts rather than extractions — 17 reports and 24 edges, already typed and with basis written as paraphrase. Two edges survived. Every quotation below was read against its own source: the OMPF Technical Guide in full, the Assessment Act via ontario.ca e-Laws, MPAC's own pages, and alberta.ca. What failed is recorded in _dropped at the same length as what passed, because the failures are the more useful half.

reports.title: Property Assessment Notice and Assessment Roll (Current Value Assessment)
reports.description: Ontario's single province-wide property assessment, prepared by a not-for-profit corporation funded by all Ontario municipalities rather than by a government department. This is the structural difference from Alberta, where each municipality prepares its own roll and the province must then run an explicit equalization step to make them comparable. Ontario needs no equalization because there is one assessor. The standard is Current Value, defined in the Assessment Act s. 1(1) as 'the amount of money the fee simple, if unencumbered, would realize if sold at arm's length by a willing seller to a willing buyer'. MPAC states it uses 'one of three approaches to value properties: direct comparison approach, income approach, cost approach', with the direct comparison approach 'the most commonly used' and the choice depending on 'property type, and the number of recent comparable sales of similar properties in the area'. The returned roll and its household counts are what the Ontario Municipal Partnership Fund allocates against.
reports.cadence_note: The roll returns annually; the values in it have not been re-based since 2016, and the gap between those two facts is the point. The Assessment Act s. 19.2(1) sets a four-year cycle by schedule, and para 4 assigns 1 January 2016 to 'the four taxation years from 2017 to 2020'. MPAC states the schedule has been suspended: 'On August 16, 2023, the Ontario government filed a regulation to amend the Assessment Act, extending the postponement of a province-wide reassessment through the end of the 2021-2024 assessment cycle. Property assessments for the 2026 property tax year will continue to be based on fully phased-in January 1, 2016 current values.' So `releases_per_year` 1 counts the returned roll, which does move for new construction, demolition and change of use; `changes_per_year` 0.25 is the statutory reassessment cycle, which is the rate at which the valuation basis is supposed to move and has not moved in ten years. Both numbers are true and neither alone describes this node.

entries.covers: 2023 Property Assessment Notices mailed (Nov) and Assessment Roll returned (Dec 12, 2023)
2024 Property Assessment Notices mailed (Nov, 627,000+ notices) and Assessment Roll returned (Dec 10, 2024)
2025 Property Assessment Notices mailed and Assessment Roll returned (fact sheet dated Dec 9, 2025)
Projected 2026 Property Assessment Notices and Assessment Roll return, based on the consistent Nov-Dec annual pattern

release_schedule.note: MPAC delivers an assessment roll annually to Ontario municipalities each Nov-Dec (with Property Assessment Notices mailed to owners with changed assessments in November, and the roll formally 'returned' in early-mid December: Dec 12 2023, Dec 10 2024, ~Dec 9 2025). This annual notice/roll cycle is distinct from the province-wide Current Value Assessment (CVA) base-year update: Ontario's Assessment Act nominally requires reassessment on a 4-year cycle, but the government has repeatedly postponed it by regulation since 2020 (most recently confirmed through the 2026 tax year), so assessed values remain frozen at January 1, 2016 current values with no announced date for the next province-wide reassessment. The annual roll-return/notice cycle, however, has continued on schedule every year regardless of the reassessment freeze.

reports.title: Ontario Municipal Partnership Fund — Allocations and Technical Guide
reports.description: Ontario's main unconditional transfer to municipalities, described in its own Technical Guide as 'the Province's main general assistance grant to municipalities'. The 2026 programme provides 'a total of $600 million in unconditional funding to 388 municipalities' through four core grant components plus Transitional Assistance. It earns a place in this graph for a reason unrelated to its size: the Technical Guide carries an Appendix F headed 'Data sources', a literal table of every data element the allocation formula consumes and where each one comes from. Documents that name their own inputs in a table are the strongest evidence class this project recognises, and they are rare outside statute.

entries.covers: 2027 OMPF allocations and technical guide (projected next edition)

release_schedule.note: The Ontario Ministry of Finance does not publish a fixed release calendar or a statutory deadline for OMPF allocations/technical guide. The ministry states only that 'OMPF allocations are announced annually in time to support the municipal budget planning process' (per the 2026 technical guide page). Observed history: 2024 guide published 2023-10-20; 2025 guide published 2024-10-30; 2026 guide published 2025-10-31 — a consistent late-October release each year for the following calendar year's allocations. The next edition (2027 OMPF) is therefore projected for late October 2026, but no exact day is confirmed.

reports.title: Financial Information Return (FIR)
reports.publisher: Ontario Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing
reports.description: Ontario's mandatory annual municipal financial return — the direct counterpart of `ab-municipalaffairs-fir`, already a node in this graph for Alberta. The FIR portal describes it as 'a standardized reporting of a municipality's financial activities in the previous fiscal year (January to December)', collecting data on assets, liabilities, revenue, expenses and statistical information drawn from each municipality's audited financial statements. Mandatory under the Municipal Act s. 294(1): 'the treasurer of a municipality shall in each year provide the Minister with a return containing information designated by the Minister with respect to the financial affairs of the municipality.' Named directly in the OMPF Technical Guide's Appendix F: 'PIL Weighted Assessment | 2023 or 2024 | Municipal FIR (Financial Information Return)'. Minted 2026-08-09 (corpus-wide `_dropped` sweep, Tier-1 item #7).
reports.cadence_note: Annual, deadline 31 May per the FIR portal's own description of the submission cycle; collected since 1978 (covering 1977 financial data), with complete province-wide datasets from 1988 onward per the portal's own historical archive.

release_schedule.rule: The deadline for the completion of the [year] Financial Information Return (FIR) is May 31 of the following year (e.g., "The deadline for the completion of 2025 FIR is May 31, 2026"), per the FIR Instructions issued by the Ontario Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing under Municipal Act s.294(1).
release_schedule.note: The 2025 FIR deadline of May 31, 2026 has already passed as of 2026-08-11; next occurrence is the 2026 FIR, due May 31, 2027, following the same annual pattern. Deadline is stated in the annual FIR Instructions document (page 9, 'Deadline for Completion' section) rather than a fixed statutory date, but has been consistently May 31 in recent years.

reports.title: Spatial Data Infrastructure (SDI)
reports.description: The geographic reference database behind Statistics Canada's published boundary and road-network products, named directly in the OMPF Technical Guide's Appendix F ('Municipal Land Area is based on the Spatial Data Infrastructure (SDI) from Statistics Canada and excludes bodies of water') but never itself released. Statistics Canada's own Illustrated Glossary describes it as 'an internal maintenance database that is not disseminated outside of Statistics Canada. It contains roads, road names and address ranges from the National Geographic Database (NGD), as well as boundary arcs of standard geographic areas.' Minted 2026-08-09 as a terminus, not a research failure — it resolves the OMPF's Municipal Land Area input to a named, real thing that cannot be a node under the ordinary rule, per Research.1.md §4's terminus provisions.

reports.title: Online Property Tax Analysis System (OPTA)
reports.publisher: Information Services Corporation (ISC), for the Ontario Ministry of Finance
reports.description: The software system behind the OMPF's 'Average Annual Change in Assessment (New Construction)' indicator ('2020–2025 | Online Property Tax Analysis System (OPTA)', Appendix F). ISC's own description: 'a centralized tool that supports more than 440 municipalities across Ontario. From budget forecasting to tax rate calculations, it plays a critical role in helping local governments deliver accurate, efficient property tax services.' A property-tax administration system operated under contract for the Ministry of Finance, not a published statistical release — no edition, no title beyond the system's own name, no publication to point at. Minted 2026-08-09 as a terminus, resolving the lead this file's own text predicted ('may well turn out to be `unpublishable-source` on inspection, in the same family as the FR 2420 form behind H.15').

dependencies.basis: 2026 OMPF Technical Guide, Appendix F 'Data sources', which names MPAC in three of its twelve rows: 'Weighted Assessment | 2025 Returned Roll and 2026 starting tax ratios | Municipal Property Assessment Corporation (MPAC) and municipal tax rate bylaws'; 'Number of Households | 2025 | MPAC (Municipal Property Assessment Corporation) Returned Roll'; and 'Farm Land Area | 2024 | MPAC (Municipal Property Assessment Corporation) and Ontario Parcel'. The guide body states the dependency again in prose for the farm measure: the land 'must be assessed and valued as farm land by the Municipal Property Assessment Corporation (MPAC)'. This is a named organisation *and* a named product — the Returned Roll — which is what distinguishes it from the five agency-only Statistics Canada rows in the same table that were declined. Weighted Assessment per Household is also the primary indicator in the Municipal Fiscal Circumstances Index, so this is not a peripheral input: it is the measure the allocation turns on.

reference_period.stated_as: Annual, but the three MPAC rows read three different vintages in the same allocation year: Weighted Assessment takes the '2025 Returned Roll and 2026 starting tax ratios', Number of Households takes 2025, and Farm Land Area takes 2024 — the guide specifying 'acres of land for properties in the farm property tax class, as of December 31st, 2024'. `ends` is null rather than 12-31 because that date governs only the farm row. One edge carrying three reading dates is a limitation of the model recorded rather than smoothed over.

dependencies.basis: NARROW, AND THE NARROWNESS IS THE FINDING. Appendix F attributes six separate indicators to 'Statistics Canada' and names no release for any of them, which is agency-level attribution and the same test that removed `boc-mpr -> statcan-national-accounts` in V0.9 and killed the H.15 restoration in V0.10. Five of the six are therefore declined and recorded in _dropped. Exactly one names a publication, in Appendix G's definition of the Rural and Small Community Measure: 'The measure is based on Statistics Canada data from the 2021 Census.' That is a named recurring release and it carries this edge, alone. The basis is written this way because the edge would otherwise be read as covering all six, and a later pass finding the other five undocumented would think this edge had been demoted rather than that it had always been this narrow. STRUCTURAL NOTE: this single sentence is also the only documented link between Ontario and the rest of the corpus. Without it the two nodes in this slice would form a second connected component, breaking an invariant held since V0.8. The graph stays at one component on the strength of one clause in an appendix definition.

OMPF Technical Guide Appendix F: 'PIL Weighted Assessment | 2023 or 2024 | Municipal FIR (Financial Information Return)'. Named by title and abbreviation together, unlike the six Statistics Canada agency-only rows in the same table. Part of the same Appendix F pass that produced the mpac-assessment and statcan-census-population edges above.

OMPF Technical Guide Appendix F: 'Municipal Land Area is based on the Spatial Data Infrastructure (SDI) from Statistics Canada and excludes bodies of water.' A named product, now modelled as a terminus (see statcan-spatial-data-infrastructure's own terminal_reason) rather than left as an unmintable lead.

OMPF Technical Guide Appendix F: 'Average Annual Change in Assessment (New Construction) | 2020–2025 | Online Property Tax Analysis System (OPTA)'. Named by title; now modelled as a terminus (see on-opta's own terminal_reason) rather than left as an unmintable lead.

_dropped.why: The submitted artifact proposed this with the basis that Employment Rate is a 'Statistics Canada measure of employed persons ÷ population aged 15+'. Appendix G says exactly that and no more: 'Employment Rate — Statistics Canada's measure of number of employed persons, divided by persons aged 15 and over.' No release is named, so it fails on agency-only grounds before the target is even considered. It also fails on the target: Appendix F dates the Employment Rate to 2021 alongside the other Census-year indicators, and a municipality-level employment rate for 388 municipalities is a Census product, not a Labour Force Survey one — the LFS is a monthly sample that does not publish at that geography. Filed `wrong-target` rather than `no-document` because the underlying dependency is real and almost certainly runs to the Census; what is missing is a document saying so. If a later pass finds one, this becomes a second Census edge, not an LFS edge. RE-CHECKED 2026-08-09 (sweep session, Tier-1 item #7) — re-fetched the Technical Guide's own Appendix F/G text directly; the 2021 dating and Statistics-Canada-only attribution are both confirmed exactly as before, and no document naming Census or LFS specifically was found. No change.

AGENCY ONLY, five times over, in a table whose entire purpose is to disclose sources. Appendix F attributes Median Household Income, Per Cent of Population Above Low-Income Threshold, Ratio of Working Age to Dependent Population, Employment Rate and Municipal Land Area to 'Statistics Canada' with no publication named, and Appendix G's definitions repeat the pattern in prose — 'Statistics Canada's measure of median income for all private households in 2020', 'the Statistics Canada measure of the population in private households above the low-income threshold', 'Statistics Canada's measure of working age population (aged 15 to 64)'. All five are plainly Census 2021 products to anyone who works with this data, and that is exactly why they are not edges. This is the H.15 finding in a provincial grant formula: a thoroughly-disclosing document whose disclosure stops one level short of a title. Worth recording as a corpus fact, because the OMPF is otherwise the best-disclosing municipal funding document found so far and it still fails five times out of six. RE-CHECKED 2026-08-09 — one of the five, Municipal Land Area, is now resolved differently: it names something more specific than 'Statistics Canada' (the Spatial Data Infrastructure), so it has moved out of this bucket into its own now-minted terminus below. Four remain in this bucket, not five; text left otherwise unchanged since the remaining four are still bare agency attributions.

RESOLVED 2026-08-09 (sweep session, Tier-1 item #7) — minted as a terminus, `statcan-spatial-data-infrastructure`, kind `confidential`. The genuine question this entry raised — 'the node rule meets a reference product rather than a periodical' — is answered for this specific case by the terminus mechanism rather than by stretching the ordinary node rule: the SDI is real, named and load-bearing, and cannot be a node because it is deliberately never released, which is exactly what a terminus is for. Appendix F names it alongside MPAC in the Farm Land Area row: 'MPAC (Municipal Property Assessment Corporation) and Ontario Parcel'. Ontario Parcel is a mapping dataset jointly maintained by the province, MPAC and Teranet. Same category question as the SDI above — a geographic reference product rather than a recurring release. Two of these arriving in one document is enough to notice that municipal funding formulas consume geography as well as statistics, and that the corpus currently has no way to represent that. RE-CHECKED 2026-08-09 (sweep session, Tier-1 item #7) — unlike the SDI, this one did NOT resolve the same way. Confirmed real and titled ('a standardized, Ontario-wide, geospatial dataset of assessment, ownership and Crown parcels of land', per Ontario's own GeoHub) and confirmed the joint maintainers by name (Ministry of Northern Development, Mines, Natural Resources and Forestry; MPAC; Teranet Enterprises Inc., under a tripartite agreement since 2002, per Teranet's own page) — but no update-frequency statement was found on either the GeoHub or Teranet pages, so the cadence condition Research.1.md §4 requires is still unmet. Genuinely still open, not stale; a future session needs a third source (the tripartite agreement itself, or a metadata/lineage page) rather than a repeat of these two searches.

A THIRD STATUTE THAT ANTICIPATES ITS OWN SUSPENSION, and the submitted artifact had the outcome right and the mechanism wrong. It attributed the 2016 valuation date for the 2026 taxation year to 'successive postponements', citing nothing. The Act's own schedule says something narrower. Assessment Act s. 19.2(1) para 4: 'For the period consisting of the four taxation years from 2017 to 2020, land is valued as of January 1, 2016', and para 5 provides that after 2020 each four-year period is valued as of 'January 1 of the year that precedes the period by two years'. Read alone, the Act does not put 2016 anywhere near 2026. The bridge is s. 19.2(5): 'Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of the valuation of land for a taxation year after 2004 if the Minister prescribes a different day as of which land is valued for that year.' MPAC confirms that is what happened — a regulation filed 16 August 2023. So the statute contains a clause permitting its own timetable to be set aside, and that clause has now been used to hold a valuation date six years past the schedule it was written into. This belongs with the Canada Pension Plan Act's splice clause and the Oil Sands Royalty Regulation's provision for the day the Bank of Canada stops publishing an exchange rate: three instances now, and enough to call it a pattern rather than a curiosity. Legislation about numbers routinely writes in what to do when the number stops behaving, and the graph has no way to show it. READ 2026-08-09 — still correct, no change.

PROCESS FINDING, recorded because the format question was settled in V0.9 and this is the first regression. V0.9 established that a second reader extracts and this project adjudicates: no verdict field, verbatim quotes, `AGENCY ONLY` where only an institution is named. Three rounds in V0.10 under that format produced zero adjudication errors. This artifact arrived in the pre-V0.9 shape — 17 finished report objects and 24 finished edges with `relationship_type` already chosen and `basis` written as paraphrase rather than quotation. Two edges of the twenty-four survived. The paraphrasing is what did the damage: not one of the twelve Equalization bases contains a quoted string, so there was nothing to check against the source except the section number, and the section numbers were the ones already known to be wrong. Where the artifact did quote — the Appendix F rows, the Assessment Act current-value definition — it was accurate, and those are the parts that became edges. The rule holds and has now been tested from the other side: a verbatim quote is checkable in minutes, a paraphrase is not checkable at all. It also under-reported its own best source. Appendix F names twelve data elements; the artifact used three of them, ignored Municipal FIR, OPTA and Ontario Parcel entirely, and spent its effort on the six Statistics Canada rows that name no release. READ 2026-08-09 — still correct; worth noting that this session's own mints (FIR, SDI terminus, OPTA terminus) are exactly the three the artifact 'ignored entirely', confirming the process finding's point that quoted, tabular sources are more productive than a paraphrasing reader's own judgement calls.
